behavior: AuthServiceClient refuses to send any request unless AUTH_SERVICE_URL and RH_AUTH_SERVICE_REQUEST_TOKEN are set and the URL starts with https:// (raises AuthServiceNotConfigured).

Any response whose status or error_code is MFA_REQUIRED/OTP_REQUIRED/DEVICE_APPROVAL_NEEDED, or whose detail mentions 'device approval', logs 'OTP needed' and raises OTPRequired. This is checked before the HTTP status code.
proof: Stub box 409 {error_code:'DEVICE_APPROVAL_NEEDED'}; expect OTPRequired, not AuthServiceError.

behavior: auth_status() converts OTPRequired into {authenticated:false, otp_needed:true}; every other call raises.
proof: Same stub as ac-otp-detection; auth_status returns dict.

behavior: get_box_token is sqlite-first (meta table in STOP_DB_PATH): it calls box GET /token only when the cached token is missing, has no expiry, is within 300s of expiry, or force=True. It never raises; it returns None on OTP or any box error.

The client timeout (AUTH_SERVICE_TIMEOUT 30s) is far shorter than the box's auth wait (CALLER_TIMEOUT 200s, APPROVAL_DEADLINE 180s). A /token or /login that needs a device push times out client-side, gets cached as 'no token', and is retried next tick while the box keeps waiting.
proof: Revoke the RH session; client.login() raises AuthServiceError (ReadTimeout) at ~30s while journalctl shows the box still awaiting approval.

behavior: DIRECT_ALLOW_LIST is declared (GET/POST /orders/trailing_stop) but nothing reads it; the client sends get_option_positions, get_order, cancel_order, etc. regardless.
proof: git grep DIRECT_ALLOW_LIST -> single definition, no uses.

behavior: get_order calls GET /orders/{id}, which the box doesn't route (404 -> AuthServiceError). A live walk_order therefore fails at its first lookup.
notes: Code comment acknowledges: 'need matching box routes (auth-service task)'.

behavior: cancel_order calls POST /orders/{id}/cancel, which the box doesn't route. The idempotent-cancel handler treats any '404' as already-gone, so every live cancel reports {already_gone:true} success without cancelling anything.
proof: Against the real box: cancel_order('<open id>', dry_run=False) returns already_gone:true and the order is still open in RH.
notes: The test stubs a 404 and asserts success, which locks in the false positive.

behavior: The module docstring lists POST /orders/options/limit ('when deployed'), but neither the client nor the box implements it.
replace_order goes through POST /orders/trailing_stop/replace, where the box guardrail requires trigger=stop and a percentage trailing_peg. Walking a plain limit order gets 403 GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED.
proof: replace_order on a payload built from a limit order (trigger:'immediate') -> AuthServiceError 403 GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED.

behavior: build_replace_payload copies immutable fields, overrides price/quantity, and mints a fresh ref_id unless one is passed. Retries must reuse ref_id or RH stacks duplicate orders. walk_order chains onto each replacement's new id and does a single step when dry_run.

mcp_relay/mcp_call send JSON-RPC to POST /exec/mcp. The box blocks tools/call whose name has a destructive verb token unless it contains 'trailing' or is in [mcp] allowed_tools. MCP-level failures return ok:false with error_code instead of raising.
verified_by: pytest auth-service/tests/test_guardrails.py (60 passed w/ session_verify, server)

behavior: If no MCP OAuth token is configured, the box falls back to the live RH password-session access token for /exec/mcp.
proof: Unset MCP_TOKEN/MCP_TOKEN_SECRET; relay succeeds using the RH bearer.

behavior: The box serves a cached token only if it is unexpired AND verified against Robinhood (GET /user/, throttled to every 300s per token; failures are never cached). /auth/status reports authenticated by verification, not by the clock. Added after the 2026-08-04 revocation incident.
Box re-auth spends the cached refresh_token first (silent, no push); only on refresh failure does it do a full login with a device push. Concurrent callers join one in-flight auth per profile.
proof: journalctl -u auth-service shows 'token refreshed for rh.auth (no push)'.

behavior: The session.py docstring says CALLER_TIMEOUT 100s / APPROVAL_DEADLINE 90s, but the code sets 200s / 180s.
When the box can't build a session, read routes return 409 with the raw exception text in detail (e.g. GCP metadata host and URL) to any bearer-holding caller.
proof: Local box with no GCP creds: GET /positions/options -> 409 detail='HTTPConnectionPool(host=metadata.google.internal..'.

behavior: The box resolves the route before checking auth, so an unauthenticated caller can tell unknown routes (404) from real ones (401).
